chunks: So all glory to Him who holds all power over everything, to whom you will go back in the end.

key_terms.بِيَدِهِ: In His hand (symbolizing power and control)
key_terms.تُرْجَعُونَ: You will be returned (eschatological return to God)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'bi-yadihi malakutu kulli shay' mean in Surah Yaseen?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to affirm God's absolute sovereignty (Mulk) and His direct control over the 'malakut' (the unseen realm of dominion), distinguishing His power from created forces. It underscores the inevitability of the return (Ma'ad) to the Creator, a core tenet of Shia eschatology, reminding believers that all authority ultimately converges back to Him for judgment.
